descriptors.concept_name: Balanced Scorecard - linkage between performance measures
descriptors.definition: The balanced scorecard evaluates organizational performance across financial, customer, internal, and innovation dimensions by connecting short-term goals with long-term strategy. It emphasizes mobilizing intangible assets alongside physical capital to achieve a competitive advantage in the information age.
inclusion: Human resource and brand awareness metrics
exclusion: Exclusive reliance on physical asset investments
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from traditional financial-only performance models by incorporating non-financial dimensions and intangible asset management.

descriptors.concept_name: Kaplan and Norton classified performance measures into four business perspectives
descriptors.definition: This framework divides business performance measurement into financial, customer, internal business, and learning perspectives to align operational objectives with corporate strategy. It addresses shareholder expectations while establishing lead and outcome indicators across operational and market segments.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from the Performance Pyramid by categorizing metrics into four distinct strategic perspectives rather than a hierarchical operational pyramid.

descriptors.concept_name: Why does Balanced Scorecard fail to provide the desired results
descriptors.definition: Balanced scorecards can fail when organizations mistakenly treat existing non-financial metrics as a complete scorecard, delegate implementation entirely to middle management, or copy external measures blindly. Additional pitfalls include treating the scorecard merely as an external reporting tool rather than an internal management mechanism linked to employee rewards.
inclusion: Lack of behavioral alignment with rewards
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on behavioral and structural implementation pitfalls rather than the structural design of the scorecard perspectives.

descriptors.concept_name: The following figure summarizes the ideas of a Balanced Scorecard
descriptors.definition: A balanced scorecard translates organizational strategy into actionable performance measures centered around a common strategic core. It interconnects customer, internal, financial, and innovation perspectives to maintain sustainable performance.
instrument_references: Robert S Kaplan and David P Norton
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes the visual and operational translation framework of strategy over individual perspective details.
source_ambiguities: The source text references a missing figure illustration.

descriptors.definition: Organizations link various performance measures to ensure sustainability within a hostile business environment, centered around a unified corporate strategy. This blending of financial, non-financial, internal, and external aspects ensures that measured operational areas receive managerial attention.
instrument_references: Robert S Kaplan and David P Norton
inclusion: Integration of short and long-term objectives
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the mutual reinforcement and inter-se relationships among diverse performance indicators rather than a single metric category.

descriptors.concept_name: Performance Pyramid - Link Strategy, Operations, and Performance
descriptors.definition: The Strategic Measurement Analysis and Reporting Technique (SMART) performance pyramid integrates corporate vision with operational performance dimensions through a four-level hierarchy. It links external market effectiveness with internal operational efficiency across financial and non-financial measures.
instrument_references: F. Cross and R. L. Lynch
inclusion: Financial and market CSFs at Level 2
Operational status checks for quality and cycle time at Level 4
exclusion: Inclusion of non-shareholder stakeholder groups beyond customers
nearby_distinctions: Differs from the Balanced Scorecard by utilizing a rigid hierarchical pyramid structure that focuses primarily on shareholder and customer perspectives.

descriptors.definition: This mechanism connects SBU operational activities to corporate vision, driving operational efficiency by demonstrating how worker efforts aid strategy execution. Objectives flow downward from the top while performance measures flow upward from the bottom of the pyramid.
inclusion: External non-financial and internal financial force balancing
exclusion: Uncoordinated operational tasks lacking strategic alignment
nearby_distinctions: Superior to the balanced scorecard in enforcing strict organizational level hierarchy and explicitly linking operational measures to corporate vision.

descriptors.concept_name: Link between the achievement of the corporate strategy and the management of human resources
descriptors.definition: In service industries, aligning human resource management with corporate strategy requires establishing clear, controllable standards and motivating reward systems. The building block model addresses this by linking specific staff targets to strategic goals to foster ownership, achievability, and fairness.
nearby_distinctions: Directly connects staff motivation and reward mechanisms to strategy achievement rather than relying purely on broad financial KPIs.

descriptors.definition: The Triple Bottom Line framework evaluates business decision sustainability across three dimensions: people, planet, and profit, extending traditional accounting into modern sustainability reporting. It supports meeting present needs without compromising future generations by incorporating environmental and social performance alongside financial returns.
inclusion: Environmental impact and ecological footprint measurement
Social equity, governance, and health measures
exclusion: Exclusive reliance on single-bottom-line economic profit reporting
nearby_distinctions: Extends traditional financial reporting by mandating equal evaluation of social and environmental impacts instead of focusing solely on shareholder value.

descriptors.definition: Sustainable business decisions are assessed through the interplay of planet, people, and profit dimensions, classifying outcomes into subsets such as bearable, equitable, viable, and sustainable. This stakeholder-oriented approach requires businesses to account for full costs across all three bottom lines.
nearby_distinctions: Classifies business activities based on multidimensional acceptability criteria rather than financial profitability alone.

descriptors.concept_name: Effect of quality practices on PMS and Quality-related costs
descriptors.definition: Adopting quality practices enhances performance but incurs quality costs divided into conformance costs (prevention and appraisal) and non-conformance costs (internal and external failures). Measuring these costs through a robust costing system modifies worker behavior and optimizes overall performance costs.
inclusion: Staff rewards based on quality KPIs
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates between desirable conformance investments ('good costs') and failure expenses ('bad costs') to drive targeted operational improvements.

descriptors.concept_name: Role of quality management system as sub-set or support system to PMS
descriptors.definition: A Quality Management System (QMS) directs and controls organizational performance to ensure continuous improvement, maintaining an inverse relationship between its rigor and non-conformance costs. Effective QMS implementations optimize overall quality costs, boost customer satisfaction via perceived value, and empower staff.
inclusion: QMS as a support subsystem for PMS
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an operational support subsystem that directly influences the broader Performance Management System rather than functioning as a standalone strategic framework.
